verbatim: Site 1 is situated almost in the centre of the Strand, and is the closest inshore. The site is represented by a distinct pattern of magnetometer readings covering an area 165 by 40 m, suggesting a wide scatter of ferrous remains (Fig. 1c). Due to its exposed position the site is the most dynamic of the three. Its depth varies between 3.8 and 5.2 m depending on the state of the tide and sand accretion (all depths are mean averages for the centres of the sites as indicated by magnetometer readings). Sand overburden has reached a maximum measured depth of 0.8 m above the highest known part of the wreck and at its lowest point is 1.2 m below the same point, represented by a wrought iron anchor.

Site 2. South-west of La Juliana's location, some 390 m distant, a smaller group of readings constitutes Site 2. It covers an area 15 by 10 m of high intensity magnetometer readings. The depth varies between 3.5 and 5.0 m.

Site 3. 20 m south-west from Site 2 is the largest group of readings, covering some 270 m by 72 m. The depth of water recorded on the site varies between 3.8 and 5.0 m depending on the state of the tide and the sand overburden. Monitoring of the sites indicates that Site 3 is where the maximum sand accretion occurs; this being influenced by Streedagh Point which acts as barrier to south-west wind generated swell.
